01

Executive Summary

This report documents the analysis of a suspicious email with the subject "A Hope to CoCanDa" sent to themajornearth@gmail.com. The email was analysed as part of a Blue Team Labs Online (BTLO) challenge to identify phishing indicators and attacker infrastructure.

The email exhibits multiple high-confidence phishing indicators: SPF authentication failure, mismatched Reply-To address, use of the known malicious mail relay emkei.cz, and Base64-encoded content with suspicious attachments. The sender spoofed identity of "Bill" using microapple.com — a typosquat impersonating Apple Inc.

Key Finding: The email was relayed through emkei.cz (IP: 93.99.104.210), a publicly known anonymous fake email service operational since 2009 — sender identity is entirely fabricated.

03

Authentication Analysis

SPF — Sender Policy Framework

SPF returned FAIL. Sending IP 93.99.104.210 (emkei.cz) is not an authorised sender for microapple.com — spoofing confirmed.

HEADERspf=fail (google.com: domain of billjobs@microapple.com does not
designate 93.99.104.210 as permitted sender)

DKIM — DomainKeys Identified Mail

No DKIM signature present. Email integrity and sender authorisation cannot be cryptographically verified.

DMARC

DMARC was not evaluated or enforced — emails failing SPF and DKIM may still reach inboxes.

Triple Authentication Failure: SPF FAIL + No DKIM + No DMARC. This combination is a high-confidence phishing indicator and ideal SIEM detection rule.

07

Hidden Excel Content — Sheet3

An Excel attachment contained a hidden sheet (Sheet3) with white text on a black background — a concealment technique making content invisible to casual inspection. The cells held Base64-encoded strings.

Excel Sheet3 — Hidden White-on-Black Base64 Content
BASE64 DECODED"The Martian Colony, Beside Interplanetary Spaceport."
FindingDetail
Sheet NameSheet3
ConcealmentWhite text on black background — invisible to casual viewer
EncodingBase64
Decoded ValueThe Martian Colony, Beside Interplanetary Spaceport.
Analyst ActionSelect all cells, change font colour to black to reveal
SignificanceAttacker embedded encoded lore clues across multiple file types

Tip: Always inspect all sheets in Excel attachments. Use Ctrl+A and change font colour to reveal hidden white-on-black text — common in both CTF challenges and real-world attacker tradecraft.

10

Recommendations

Immediate Actions

Block IP 93.99.104.210 and domain emkei.cz at email gateway and firewall. Add all IOC domains and emails to blocklists. Submit to VirusTotal for retroactive threat hunting.

Detection Engineering

• Alert on emails where Reply-To domain differs from From domain
• Flag emails containing "from localhost (emkei" in Received headers
• Alert on SPF FAIL + no DKIM + no DMARC triple authentication failure
• Alert on Message-ID containing @localhost

User Awareness

• Train users to verify Reply-To before responding to any email
• Educate staff on typosquatting — microapple.com vs apple.com
• Implement mail client banners for external emails with mismatched Reply-To
• Train analysts to inspect all Excel sheets for hidden or white-coloured text
